title: Medicare Part B Premium 2026 and IRMAA Brackets
metaDescription: The standard Medicare Part B premium 2026 is $202.90 and the deductible is $283. Review the 2026 IRMAA brackets and Part D surcharges.
h1: Medicare Part B Premium 2026 and IRMAA Brackets
cardBlurb: The standard Medicare Part B premium 2026 is $202.90, the annual deductible is $283, and IRMAA adds monthly surcharges for higher earners.
introText:
The standard monthly Medicare Part B premium 2026 is $202.90, and the annual Part B deductible is $283. At ModernWallet, we treat this as a line item to confirm before the rest of the plan.

Higher earners pay an extra monthly surcharge called the Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount (IRMAA). Roughly 8% of people with Medicare Part B pay this adjustment, while roughly 92% pay only the standard rate. The surcharge also adds an extra charge to Part D prescription drug coverage for those same income brackets.

sections.heading: The 2026 Part B Premium and Deductible
sections.body:
The standard monthly Medicare Part B premium 2026 is $202.90, and the annual Part B deductible is $283. Enrollees pay this annual deductible once per calendar year before Part B benefits begin.

Inpatient care carries separate expenses. The Medicare Part A inpatient hospital deductible is $1,736 per benefit period admission in 2026.

[CMS](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/2026-medicare-parts-b-premiums-deductibles) announced these official amounts on November 14, 2025. If you wait to sign up when you must pay for Part B, you may pay a monthly late enrollment penalty for as long as you have Part B, and it goes up the longer you wait. To review the timelines for signing up, read our guide to [medicare enrollment periods](/guides/medicare-enrollment-periods/).

sections.heading: IRMAA Eligibility and Affected Enrollees
sections.body:
The Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount (IRMAA) is an extra monthly charge added to standard Part B and Part D premiums for higher-income enrollees. Roughly 8% of people with Medicare Part B pay this adjustment. Roughly 92% of enrollees pay only the standard rate without any income surcharge.

Social Security determines IRMAA from the most recent federal tax return provided for your account. For 2026 premium amounts, Social Security generally uses a return filed in 2025 for tax year 2024. If your reported income exceeds the base threshold on that return, you pay an adjusted rate for the entire year.

The joint thresholds apply to married filing jointly. Other filing statuses, such as married filing separately, have different rules that are not listed on the official fact sheet. If you file under another status, confirm your specific bracket with Social Security.

sections.heading: The Six 2026 IRMAA Tiers
sections.body:
Medicare sets six income tiers that establish the monthly Part B and Part D surcharges. Social Security places each enrollee into a tier based on modified adjusted gross income.

- **Tier 1:** Individual filers with income of $109,000 or less, and joint filers with income of $218,000 or less. The Part B adjustment is $0.00, so the total Part B monthly premium is $202.90. The Part D monthly adjustment is $0.00.
- **Tier 2:** Individual filers with income above $109,000 to $137,000, and joint filers with income above $218,000 to $274,000. The Part B monthly adjustment is $81.20, so the total Part B monthly premium is $284.10. The Part D monthly adjustment is $14.50.
- **Tier 3:** Individual filers with income above $137,000 to $171,000, and joint filers with income above $274,000 to $342,000. The Part B monthly adjustment is $202.90, so the total Part B monthly premium is $405.80. The Part D monthly adjustment is $37.50.
- **Tier 4:** Individual filers with income above $171,000 to $205,000, and joint filers with income above $342,000 to $410,000. The Part B monthly adjustment is $324.60, so the total Part B monthly premium is $527.50. The Part D monthly adjustment is $60.40.
- **Tier 5:** Individual filers with income above $205,000 to under $500,000, and joint filers with income above $410,000 to under $750,000. The Part B monthly adjustment is $446.30, so the total Part B monthly premium is $649.20. The Part D monthly adjustment is $83.30.
- **Tier 6:** Individual filers with income of $500,000 or more, and joint filers with income of $750,000 or more. The Part B monthly adjustment is $487.00, so the total Part B monthly premium is $689.90. The Part D monthly adjustment is $91.00.

For an individual in the second tier, the Part B adjustment is $81.20 a month and the Part D adjustment is $14.50 a month. If both apply for 12 months: $1,148.40. That extra yearly cost is paid on top of the standard Part B premium and your private drug plan premium.

sections.heading: Income Changes and Tier Thresholds
sections.body:
IRMAA tier thresholds operate as cliffs where one dollar of income above a cutoff moves you into the next tier. The official tiers use strict cutoffs, so a single dollar over a boundary triggers the full surcharge for that bracket.

Roth conversions and retirement withdrawals may change reported income, so ask a CPA how distributions affect your tax return. If you plan to convert traditional retirement assets, review our guide to [Roth conversion rules](/guides/roth-conversion-rules/) before scheduling transactions.

You can also map out your retirement distributions with our [retirement income calculator](/retirement/retirement-income-calculator/) or evaluate your baseline benefit with our [Social Security retirement calculator](/retirement/social-security-retirement-calculator/).

sections.heading: Costs Not Covered by Standard Part B
sections.body:
The standard Part B premium and deductible do not cover supplemental insurance or private plan costs. Medicare Advantage, Medigap, Part D plan premiums, and copays vary by plan.

The Part D IRMAA surcharge is added directly to whatever base premium your private prescription drug plan charges. If you want to evaluate coverage options, review our guides on [Medicare vs Medicare Advantage](/compare/medicare-vs-medicare-advantage/) and [Medicare Advantage vs Medigap](/compare/medicare-advantage-vs-medigap/).

Verify specific private plan premiums, copays, and deductibles at Medicare.gov or directly through your plan administrator.

sections.heading: Next Steps and Verification
sections.body:
You can verify your 2026 Medicare premium by checking the notice you get from Social Security. That letter shows your exact monthly Part B premium and identifies any IRMAA surcharge applied to your coverage.

If you plan to transition away from work this year, explore our walkthrough on [how to retire at 67](/guides/how-to-retire-at-67/). Check your recent tax filings with a licensed CPA or financial advisor to see where your income sits relative to the 2026 IRMAA brackets.

This guide is for educational purposes only and does not provide individualized financial, tax, insurance, or retirement advice. Confirm your specific costs, tax return details, and coverage options with Social Security, Medicare.gov, a licensed insurance agent, or a CPA.

faqs.question: What is the Medicare Part B premium in 2026?
faqs.answer: The standard monthly Medicare Part B premium 2026 is $202.90. Roughly 92% of enrollees pay this standard rate. Higher-income enrollees pay an additional monthly surcharge called IRMAA, which can increase the total monthly Part B premium up to $689.90 based on reported income.

faqs.question: What is the Part B deductible in 2026?
faqs.answer: The annual Medicare Part B deductible is $283 in 2026. Enrollees pay this deductible amount before Medicare Part B begins coverage for medical services.

faqs.question: What income triggers IRMAA in 2026?
faqs.answer: In 2026, IRMAA applies to individuals with modified adjusted gross income above $109,000 and married couples filing jointly with modified adjusted gross income above $218,000. Surcharges increase across five higher income tiers, reaching maximum monthly additions for individuals at or above $500,000 and joint filers at or above $750,000.

faqs.question: Do married couples have higher IRMAA thresholds?
faqs.answer: Married couples who file jointly have higher thresholds than single filers for each IRMAA tier. For example, Tier 1 applies to joint incomes of $218,000 or less, compared to $109,000 or less for individual filers. The joint thresholds apply to married filing jointly, so enrollees using other tax filing statuses should confirm their rules with Social Security.

faqs.question: Is the Part D IRMAA separate from the Part B IRMAA?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Part D IRMAA is a separate monthly adjustment added to your private Part D plan premium. In 2026, monthly Part D surcharges range from $14.50 in Tier 2 to $91.00 in Tier 6. You pay this surcharge in addition to any Part B surcharge that applies to your income level.
